messages:
maya (support): Heads-up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on /v1/generate since ~08:20 PT. Symptoms: long queue wait, 502/504s, and lots of 'inflight concurrency' rejects. Customers: acme-corp, betalabs.

alex (eng-runtime): Thanks — any repro request ids or traces? Do we see admission-control logs? :eyes:

maya (support): Pasted a short sample from acme: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:21:12Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-4x seq_len=512 queue_wait_ms=2200 worker_id=worker-17 admit_rejected=true token_cost=120
[2026-03-17T08:21:13Z] request_id=def456 model=redwood-4x seq_len=256 queue_wait_ms=1850 worker_id=worker-17 error=timeout
```

jamie (eng-sre): Queue_wait_ms numbers are large — looks like workers are saturated. Any recent deploys to serving? deploy-bot, any alerts?

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary redwood-4x v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 started at 2026-03-17T07:58:03Z.

dan (eng-oncall): I see spike in concurrency per-worker around 08:18-08:25 PT, plus a rise in client retries (auth failures retried by clients). Might be a combo: transient auth/billing failures causing retry storms that push admission control over the limit.

zoe (customer-success): Acme says they saw a burst after billing webhook returned 429 for a short window and their SDK retried aggressively. They attached an example: "billing: quota_exceeded" followed by exponential retries.

alex (eng-runtime): That matches. When external 429s cause client retries, our admission control sees sudden fanout. We should check auth logs for 401/403/429 trends and correlate with provider-side billing events. Also check batching thresholds — big batched requests can block workers longer.

jamie (eng-sre): Running quick checks: `kubectl top pods` shows two pods on node gpu-3 at 98% GPU mem and high CPU. Map of active streams shows worker-17 and worker-19 at full concurrency.

alex (eng-runtime): Repro steps I ran locally: 50 concurrent clients retrying on 429 -> queue depth grows, per-request queue_wait_ms climbs, admission starts rejecting (admit_rejected=true) which causes some requests to fail early but overall increases client retries.

maya (support): Customers need mitigation now — what can we do quickly to reduce p99?

dan (eng-oncall): Short term options (pick 1+):
- Whitelist tokens for affected customers so their auth check bypasses the slow external billing check.
- Temporarily increase per-worker concurrency limit (adm allow extra inflight) for the cluster to drain backlog.
- Scale up workers (add 2 hot pods) and move canary back if it's causing pressure.
- Enable fallback model (lower-cost variant) for traffic routing to reduce per-token time.

alex (eng-runtime): I can flip routing to fallback model for acme/betalabs in the router policy (canary routing override). That reduces average worker time ~30%. I'll coordinate with dan before scaling or whitelist.

jamie (eng-sre): I'll spin two extra worker pods on the dedicated pool and watch eviction windows. Command: `k scale deployment/worker-pool --replicas=12` (doing now).

alex (eng-runtime): Also temporarily relax admission control from 8 -> 12 inflight per worker for 10m: patch applied. We should watch tail latencies — admits might increase overall p50 but p99 should drop as queueing reduces.

deploy-bot: [scale] deployment/worker-pool scaled to 12 replicas by jamie at 2026-03-17T08:29:10Z.

leo (acme-corp): Thanks team — we see immediate improvement, p99 down from ~6s to ~1.8s. We'll pause client retries for 15m as requested.

zoe (customer-success): Noted — I'll confirm with other customers. Acme is okay with fallback model for the short term.

maya (support): Logging summary for incident ticket created (#INC-2026-0317-42). Added traces: abc123, def456.

alex (eng-runtime): Action items: 
- (alex) keep fallback routing for affected tenants for 30m and then gradual rollback.
- (jamie) monitor GPU mem and scale down if stable.
- (dan) investigate why billing webhook returned 429s and whether we can surface guidance to customers about retry backoff.
- (zoe) confirm customer-side changes.

jamie (eng-sre): Will run post-mortem if we see recurrence. Early hypothesis: billing-induced retry storm + recent canary increasing per-request time (v1.12.4) reduced headroom.

dan (eng-oncall): Follow-up: add a circuit-breaker to detect client-side retry storms (high retry rate per token) and fail fast with a clear 429/503 to avoid cascading. Filing an RFC.

maya (support): Customers notified and ticket updated. Marking thread for handoff to eng-sre post-incident. :thumbsup:

alex (eng-runtime): Closing note: we should add a playbook entry for "billing webhook -> retry storm" with checklist: whitelist, fallback routing, temporary scale, admit-relax. I'll draft it.

zoe (customer-success): Thanks everyone — acme confirmed recovered.

maya (support): closing thread here, will add links to incident doc and postmortem when available.
